title: Count All Possible Routes
summary: Given an array of distinct positive integers representing the positions of cities, and an initial amount of fuel, count the total number of possible routes from the starting city to the finishing city.
statement: Given an array of distinct positive integers representing the positions of cities, and an initial amount of fuel, count the total number of possible routes from the starting city to the finishing city. At each step, moving from city i to city j consumes fuel equal to the absolute difference in their positions, |locations[i] - locations[j]|. Fuel cannot drop below zero, and you may visit any city more than once. Return the total count of such routes modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: City positions are distinct; moving between cities costs their absolute coordinate distance and revisits are allowed.
Count every route that stops at finish with nonnegative fuel, including the length-zero route when start equals finish.
hints: Memoize by current city and remaining fuel.
Count one route immediately when the current city is finish, because stopping now is valid.
Try every other city whose travel cost fits and add its continuations.
Distinct positions make every move consume positive fuel, so the state graph is acyclic by remaining fuel.
